visible_prompt_profile.curated_prompt:
Arbiter.stop() does not release listening sockets on shutdown.

When the arbiter stops (gracefully or not), it must close every listening socket and unlink owned Unix socket files, then clear its listener list. Unlinking applies exactly to owned listeners: not systemd-managed sockets, not shared reuse-port sockets, and not during a re-exec handover. After releasing listeners, the arbiter terminates workers with SIGTERM, reaps them until the graceful timeout expires, and SIGKILLs stragglers.

Reproduce with the arbiter stop listener tests in tests/test_arbiter.py (stop closes listeners; child/parent/systemd/reuse-port unlink cases).
